**How to launch a digital product from zero**

1. **Research** — pick a problem you already understand. Boring beats clever.
2. **Build** — Canva for design, Notion for anything interactive.
3. **Upload** — Gumroad handles payment and delivery for you.
4. **Link** — Beacons as your storefront, one link in bio.
5. **Post** — daily, about the problem, not the product.
6. **Repeat** — the same product can sell for months.

Most people stall on step 1 for weeks. The research is not the hard part. Publishing something imperfect is.

**The whole stack costs nothing to start**

• **Claude / ChatGPT** — outline and draft
• **Canva** — design (free tier is enough)
• **Gumroad** — hosting, checkout, delivery, refunds
• **Beacons** — link in bio
• **Threads** — traffic

No website. No LLC. No inventory. No ads.

The barrier was never money. It was deciding what to make.

**A prompt that actually helps**

Paste this into Claude or ChatGPT:

_You are my content strategist. My product is [X] and it solves [problem] for [audience]. Give me 20 hooks written as statements, not questions. No engagement bait. Then give me a 7-day posting plan where 5 posts build trust and 2 mention the product._

The reason it works: it forces statements instead of questions. Questions asking for replies underperform badly on Threads.

**Pricing, honestly**

Price is not a reward for how hard you worked. It is a signal about who the product is for.

**Single digits** gets impulse buys from people who may never open it.
**Around $27** is where a stranger will take a chance on you with no reviews.
**Three figures** needs either a track record or your actual time attached.

Our own ladder runs $9, $27, $97 and $147 — cheapest is the narrow tactical guide, dearest is us doing the work for you.

Start in the middle. Move up when you have proof, not when you feel like it.

**What a normal week actually looks like**

Not the highlight version:

• Most days are quiet. Some days there are zero sales.
• The same product keeps selling with nothing new built.
• Posting feels pointless for weeks before it does not.
• The boring posts outperform the clever ones consistently.

Anyone showing you only good days is selling you something. The quiet days are most of it, and they still compound.

**The mistake that costs the most time**

Building for a month before showing anyone.

Post the idea first. Talk about the problem for a week. See if anyone responds before you build the thing.

If nobody cares about the problem, a beautiful product will not fix that. If people do care, you will build a better version because you heard them first.

Validation is a week. Building blind is a month.

**How to not run out of things to post**

Four angles, rotate them:

• **The objection** — something people say, then what actually happened
• **The contrast** — what you do not have, next to what you built anyway
• **The receipt** — a real screenshot, no exaggeration
• **The plain truth** — one sentence, no metaphor

That is four posts. Rotate them and you have a month.

You do not need new ideas. You need the same idea said plainly, often.

**Why faceless works**

You are not the product. The solution is.

No face means no personal brand to maintain, no pressure to perform, and no ceiling based on how comfortable you are on camera.

People buy the outcome. They do not need to know what you look like — they need to believe you have actually done the thing.

That is what screenshots are for. Not vanity. Evidence.

**Where the first buyers actually come from**

Not your followers. Strangers who saw one post.

Most of our sales come from people who found a single post, clicked the profile, and bought within about ten minutes. They never followed first.

That is why every post has to make sense on its own to someone who has never heard of you. No inside jokes, no 'as I mentioned yesterday'.

**The Canva part, plainly**

You do not need design skills.

• Pick a blank doc, 1080x1350
• One heading font, one body font, that is it
• Lots of white space. Crowded looks cheap
• Export as PDF

The product sells because it solves something, not because it is pretty. Pretty just stops people from asking for a refund.

**What to do when nothing sells for a week**

Do not rebuild the product. Do not lower the price.

Change the hook. Nine times out of ten the product is fine and the post is what is failing — people never got far enough to see the offer.

Write five different first lines for the same product. Post one a day. One of them will move.

**Free things are not lost revenue**

We give away a free download. It is the single best thing we made.

People who take the free thing already trust you a little. That is the hardest part of a sale, and it is done before you have asked for anything.

Give away the thing that shows you know what you are doing. Sell the thing that saves them the time.

**Posting times, from our own data**

We post six times a day and track every one.

The clear winner is late evening US time. Early morning is the worst slot by a distance — good content, nobody awake to see it.

If you only post once a day, post when your buyers are on their phone with nothing to do. Not when you happen to be free.

**Nobody is thinking about your post as much as you are**

The post you agonised over gets scrolled past in half a second.

That cuts both ways. The embarrassing one nobody remembers either. The cost of posting something imperfect is far lower than you think, and the cost of posting nothing is total.

Publish it. Fix it in version two.

**One product, priced three ways**

The same knowledge sold at three levels:

• **$27** — the file. They do it themselves.
• **$97** — two weeks of your time. You answer their questions.
• **$147** — you do the whole build for them.

Same expertise, three amounts of your time. Most people only ever build the first one and leave the other two on the table.
